M14 grammar audit (real-sql-analyzer.ts:58, the SQL_KEYWORDS set): a SQL KEYWORD in a keyword table, not a parse-tree node reference. `table` is the reserved word the guard exists to recognise, and the audit's `X.type === "lit"` / set-literal heuristic reports set members the way it reports node types. Waived, not fixed — deleting the keyword would change behaviour, and the swift `String` entry is the same shape (a type-name table, waived with a justification).

M14.0.F1 register repayment (2026-10-08, real-sql-analyzer.ts:922 adoptLateDeclaredIndexOwners): this is the symbol-metadata TAG THE ANALYZER ITSELF WRITES — `createSymbol(..., { type: "index", indexName, table, columns })` at real-sql-analyzer.ts:2380, read back as `symbol.metadata?.type !== "index"` — not a parse-tree node reference. The pinned sql grammar declares no node named `index` (its index productions are `create_index` / `alter_index` / `drop_index` / `index_fields` / `index_hint` / `keyword_index`), and no comparison in this analyzer ever tests a node against it. Waived, not fixed: deleting the comparison would drop the CREATE INDEX symbols' owner adoption, which is a behaviour change with no grammar conformance to buy. Same shape as the sql `table`/`grant_statement` and typescript `default_export_expression` entries above — an analyzer-owned payload compared against a literal, making no grammar claim. The site carries a comment saying so.

Dead by design, not by accident — the same register the swift entry uses.

M14 TS wave (real-typescript-analyzer.ts:5008, extractExportRelations): this is an ExportInfo `type` TAG THE ANALYZER WRITES ITSELF — the anonymous-default branch of extractExports sets it — not a parse-tree node reference. It is NOT a typescript grammar node type: the pinned grammar emits `export_statement` for every `export default` form, confirmed by parsing `export default f`, `export default function g(){}` and `export default 42`. The comparison suppresses the `module -> default` edge for an anonymous default export, whose target no index could ever join. Same shape as the swift String/Int entries above: a literal in a comparison against an analyzer-owned payload, making no grammar conformance claim. The name reads like a node type, which is why this tolerance is written down rather than left to look like dead code.

limitations.description: auditor detects dead references only; missing node-type coverage requires fixtures (F3) and wave work
extraction covers comparison/switch/helper-call/const-array positions; dynamic type-string construction would be missed (none observed)

the dead-literal gate is per-literal and shrink-only: it fails on a NEW literal even when the count improves, on a recorded entry with no reason, and on a recorded literal that disappears without the repayment being written down. It does not force a lane to repay registered debt — that is what wave closure criteria and the lane's completion plan are for

history (why the gate is per-literal): csharp's declared-type round added record_struct_declaration and constraint_clause on 2026-09-22 while an older finding elsewhere was fixed; the v1 count gate read 3 -> 2 as an improvement and the dead branches shipped inside a lane whose grammar cell was green

field oracle: the extractor now unwraps the `arguments` node and enumerates field ids 1..fieldCount inclusive (both bugs fixed 2026-09-16 under #382 — before that, referencedFieldLiterals was 0 in every language and the alphabetically-last field of each grammar was invisible)

REGISTERED RESIDUAL (2026-09-16, #863): with the oracle real, lua (5 sites), perl (1 site, no fallback) and r (1 site) report field literals their pinned grammar cannot resolve. Their baseline counts hold those findings; the JVM and web families are strictly clean (0 unknown field literals each)
